SUPPORTED.definition: A proposition is SUPPORTED when its substantial content is explicitly present in the supplied evidence, or is semantically implied by that evidence without adding a new assertion.
SUPPORTED.paraphrase_rule: A lexical rephrasing is not automatically an invention. A legitimate stylistic paraphrase may be SUPPORTED.
not_automatic_unsupported: stylistic intensifier that adds no agent, relation, condition, or quantity

QUESTIONABLE.definition: A proposition is QUESTIONABLE when available evidence does not confirm the whole claim; a plausible inference is not actually implied; a strengthening or substantial nuance remains uncertain; or the link to evidence is ambiguous.

UNSUPPORTED.definition: A proposition is UNSUPPORTED when it contains a substantial assertion not supported by the supplied evidence.

NON_SUBSTANTIVE.definition: A proposition is NON_SUBSTANTIVE when it is a purely rhetorical or structural marker that carries no meaning-bearing assertion.
NON_SUBSTANTIVE.not_automatic: An editorial transition is not automatically NON_SUBSTANTIVE.

INDETERMINATE.definition: A human-review category used when authorized evidence does not uniquely force SUPPORTED, QUESTIONABLE, UNSUPPORTED, or NON_SUBSTANTIVE. It is not a provider or transport value.
